messages.author: e715a3aeb27b07f3
messages.subject: log scale and zero values
parts:
Hi,
I have some dose response data including the value of a concectration
of 0.
Now, I'd like to display the data and it's fit at a plot with a log
scale. But how can I handle this first data point.
I've found a nice solution here:

http://www.graphpad.com/prism/learn/Dose-response%20curves.pdf

But, as far as I know, such plots are not possible in R. Any
suggestions how to keep this datapoint?

messages.author: 0c39e60ddb38622b
messages.subject: Re: log scale and zero values
parts:
Hi:

If you're asking whether there is a mechanism in ggplot2 to break an
axis as shown in your attached paper, there isn't. (You can't do it in
lattice either, BTW.) The only way to do this in R is to use the
plotrix package and create the plot with base graphics (see the
plotrix::axis.break() function).

HTH,
Dennis

messages.subject: Re: log scale and zero values
parts:
That graph looked terrible to me. The break seems likely to really mislead the reader but it's my area of expertise.

It seems to me that Cleveland, in his 1984 book "The Elements of Graphing Data" suggests "starting" the data by substituting a very small positive value for zero.
 Would that help?
